whatItDoes: Full scientific calculator with history, memory, and trig/log/exp functions. Standard arithmetic (+, −, ×, ÷), parentheses-free expression chaining, percent, square root, x², reciprocal, exponent (x^y), π, e, sin/cos/tan, asin/acos/atan, log (base 10), ln, 10^x, e^x, and 4-key memory (MC/MR/M+/M−). Degree and radian angle modes.
whyItExists: Browser-based scientific calculators save students, engineers, and scientists the trip to a physical calculator or the trust gap of an unvetted online one. This one is 100% client-side, has a clean history view, and supports the angle mode that matters to your work (DEG for everyday math, RAD for calculus and physics).
whoShouldUse: Students doing trig or log problems, engineers computing on the fly, scientists and statisticians who need a quick reliable calculator, and anyone who needs more than a basic pocket calculator.
useCases: Compute sin, cos, tan with one keystroke and an angle mode toggle
Use memory (M+, M−, MR) to accumulate a sum across multiple values
Square a number, take a square root, or raise to a power

Press AC to clear all history, C to clear only the current entry

Use sin/cos/tan in DEG mode for everyday math, RAD for calculus
Use log (base 10), ln (natural log), 10^x, e^x for exponential work

bestPractices: Pick the right angle mode for your problem — DEG for geometry, RAD for calculus and physics
Use memory to accumulate a sum, e.g. tap M+ after each value
Press AC to reset between unrelated calculations; C clears only the current entry
The calculator uses up to 10 significant digits, more than enough for most work
Use the history view to copy-paste results into homework or reports
commonMistakes: Forgetting to switch between DEG and RAD mode — sin(30) gives different answers
Treating %, 1/x, and x² as the same as percent of, reciprocal of, and square of
Confusing log (base 10) with ln (natural log, base e)
Expecting parentheses: this calculator does standard arithmetic only, not full expressions
Relying on long results past 10 significant digits — small floating-point error accumulates
faq: How is sin(30) different in DEG vs RAD? — In DEG mode, sin(30) = 0.5 (30 degrees). In RAD mode, sin(30) ≈ −0.988 (30 radians). The same key gives a different answer.
Is memory persistent across page reloads? — No. Memory and history live in component state, so they reset on refresh. We do not store them anywhere — privacy-first.
What is the precision? — 10 significant digits, more than a physical calculator. Displayed values round to the shortest unambiguous representation.

Can I type a full expression like 2 + 3 * 4? — No. This calculator does standard chained arithmetic: enter 2, press +, enter 3, press +, enter 4, press =. The result is 9. There is no operator-precedence parser.
What is the difference between log and ln? — log is base 10 (log₁₀), ln is the natural log (base e ≈ 2.718). Use log for engineering and pH, ln for calculus and statistics.
features: Square root, x², reciprocal, percent, sign flip
